newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Finance Dept to revise up revenue data.
newsitem.headline: S.African Finance Dept to revise up revenue data.

text.p: The South African Finance Department had miscalculated the amount of revenue it had collected in the months April to August and figures would be revised upwards, a department official told Reuters on Friday.
The official, who did not want to be identified, said a statement showing the revised figures would be released later in the day.
"There is a problem and the cumulative figure is going to be revised," the official said.
The Finance Department announced on Thursday that total revenue in August amounted to 10.145 billion rand and total revenue from April to August amounted to 50.372 billion rand.

Piet van Schaik, a director at stockbrokers Barnard Jacobs Mellet, said a Government Gazette published in August showed that total revenue up to July amounted to 45.447 billion rand -- which would bring the cumulative revenue from April to August to about 55.5 billion rand.
This would mean that revenue for the five months was ahead over 14 percent on the same period last year and not the 3.7 percent stated in the government release issued on Thursday, van Schaik said.
It would also bring total revenue to about 38 percent of the total budget of 144.9 billion rand and not 34.8 percent as originally stated.

Earlier, traders on South Africa's capital market expressed concern that the slower revenue increase in August pointed to government not being able to meet its budgeted 13.8 percent increase in revenue for the full fiscal year (April/March).
Van Schaik noted that at over 14 percent, South Africa's increased revenue target was well within budget.
